situation.summary: Tenant Ari Dalen reported washing-machine error E13 on 20 Aug 2025 and confirmed on 26 Aug that it was unusable. The landlord, Nessa Orin, took the repair through the insurer and an engineer visit was booked for 9 Sep, but on 14 Sep she said a replacement was needed, and on 19 and 21 Sep she said a new machine was ordered and delivery, fitting and disposal were arranged, with no dates given. On 24 Sep the tenant said no replacement had arrived. On 25 Sep (0 days before the decision moment) the tenant replied "Yes, the job is completed" and asked whether the washing-machine change is still happening; Northbridge has not answered that question, nor the landlord's 21 Sep quote request, and the records conflict on whether the replacement has been delivered and whether the repair was completed.
situation.task: Ask landlord Nessa Orin by email to confirm the replacement's supplier, order reference, delivery and fitting dates, who pays, and whether her 21 Sep quote request still stands; send tenant Ari Dalen a same-turn email saying the replacement status is being confirmed with the landlord, with no date promised beyond the follow-up date. Do not send a quote or instruct a contractor, since the landlord says she has arranged it.

situation.whoseMove: Northbridge (Mara Venn) is holding the move. Follow-up for both parties by Monday 29 Sep 2025.

risks.description: Tenant has had no working washing machine since about 26 Aug 2025 (roughly a month). They report hand-washing and laundry waiting (E007, E013). This is a habitability and welfare concern, not a safety one.

Tenant expressed frustration at the delay (E013). Landlord complained the response took too long (E029). This is not a formal complaint or a request for compensation. Reply directly, acknowledge the delay and give a firm follow-up date. Escalate only if they ask for a manager, compensation or a formal complaint.

Who pays for the replacement is not recorded. Insurer, landlord and tenant are all possible. Do not approve, quote, or let anyone assume a cost falls on the tenant. A quote request (E028) is still unanswered.
The tenant's 'job is completed' (E031) conflicts with the record of a replacement not yet delivered (E030). Closing or reporting completion on that message would be wrong.

Fit is unconfirmed: the space is about 835 mm, the unit is 825 mm, the existing unit is integrated, and the rear connections were not checked (E025, E026). Installation with water and electrical connections should be done by the installer. No advice is given here.

decision.actionLabel: Ask tenant Ari Dalen what "the job is completed" means: is there now a working washing machine (old one repaired, or new one fitted), and please forward the other email about the planned machine change
decision.message:
Dear Ari,

Thank you for your email this morning, and I'm sorry this has taken so long to sort out.

I'd like to be sure I understand you correctly. When we spoke yesterday (24 September) you told me no replacement machine had arrived. Today you say the job is completed. Could you confirm which of these applies:

1. The existing washer-dryer has been repaired and now works normally (no E13 error); or
2. A new washing machine has been delivered and fitted, and it works; or
3. Something else (for example, the engineer visited but the machine still does not work).

If a machine is now working, please tell me roughly when that happened and who did the work.

You also mentioned that you received another email about a planned washing-machine change. Please forward it to me so I can check who sent it. I am confirming with your landlord now whether the replacement is still going ahead, and I will update you on that by Monday 29 September.

Please reply by Friday 26 September if you can. If the machine stops working or shows the error again in the meantime, let me know straight away.

Kind regards,
Mara Venn
Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings
decision.rationale: The landlord is handling this herself: she said a replacement was ordered and that delivery, fitting and disposal were arranged (E027, E029). We should not assign a contractor or send a quote. The tenant's latest message (E031) says "Yes, the job is completed", but the day before they told us no replacement had arrived (E030). The engineer visit on 9 Sep has no recorded outcome (E021, E022), and the landlord later said a replacement was needed (E023). We can't close the job, tell the landlord it is done, or answer whether the change is still happening until we know what the tenant means. Only the tenant can tell us whether a machine now works. The landlord gave no delivery date and has an unanswered quote request (E028) that her later message may have replaced (E029). She also complained about delay. So in the same turn she gets a status update with the specific questions. That answers her complaint as a routine matter and confirms the replacement's status, rather than us guessing.
decision.expectedOutcome: The tenant confirms whether a working machine is in place and forwards the other email. The landlord confirms whether the replacement is still going ahead, with delivery and fitting dates, and whether she still wants a quote. We can then tell each party the confirmed position, or move towards closing.

This does not settle who pays for the replacement (insurer or landlord), and it approves no spend.
